newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tankan won't alter economic view - BOJ Osaka manager.
newsitem.headline: Tankan won't alter economic view - BOJ Osaka manager.

text.p: The results of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) June "tankan" corporate survey will not alter the central bank's current assessment of the economy, the BOJ's Osaka branch manager Eichiro Kinoshita said on Friday.

"It's natural for business conditions of manufacturers to have shown an improvement. But that improvement has not spread to the overall (economy) or strengthened the feeling of (economic) recovery," Kinoshita said.
He said there was no need for the central bank to alter its current assessment of the economy because of the tankan.
"There are still many bearish factors," he said.

Kinoshita, who is also one of the executive directors of the central bank said pessimistic views over private consumption had emerged in June and that he was not sure to what extent production will increase in the July to September quarter from the previous quarter.
Kinoshita also said the BOJ's current monetary policy of keeping interest rates low was still necessary.

"How low interest rates should be is a separate issue altogether, but at the moment, low interest rates are needed. As domestic demand is not strong enough, basically, there is a meaning for the low rate policy," he said.
